content:
carlos: FYI customer reports Google OAuth fails only on Safari iOS webview inside their app. Works in Chrome & Safari desktop.

sam (support): What error do they see? Any logs from our callback service?

carlos: They get a 403 from our callback handler: "state verification failed". No pkce errors. Repro steps below.

elaine: Can you paste the raw redirect URL hitting our callback? Safari sometimes moves fragments into query or mangles encodings.

carlos: Here is what we captured from their proxy logs (sanitized):

GET /auth/callback?code=4/ABCDEFG&state=E2%2526F%3D%2Bxyz HTTP/1.1
Host: callback.customer.example
Referer: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth#_=_
User-Agent: SafariViewController/605.1.15

sam (support): I see double-encoding: state was %2526 (i.e. literal %26 after decode). Also note the hash fragment from Google (#_=_). Some webviews move fragments into the query; other proxies re-encode them. That will break our state compare if we expected original raw.

mike (sre): Another wrinkle: customer domain is an internationalized domain (xn--caf-dma.example). Safari's punycode handling can cause path normalization on redirect which some proxies then canonicalize, changing percent-encoding. We had a bug where we canonicalize query before validating state.

carlos: Repro steps I used:
1) Open app webview on iOS 16.4;
2) Start Google OAuth with PKCE (S256);
3) Approve; get redirected through analytics proxy (redirector.example) which appends utm params and does a 302 to our callback;
4) Our callback returns 403 (state mismatch).

elaine: Could analytics proxy be URL-encoding the incoming fragment or encoding plus -> space? Many proxies convert "+" to space when decoding form-encoded payload. Example: original state had a "+" in base64 urlsafe pad. If proxy turns + -> space then re-encodes, we see mismatch.

sam (support): Can we get their raw network capture? If not, ask them to try an incognito Safari (no SSO cookies) and also test with a direct redirect (no analytics proxy). If direct works, we can blame proxy behavior.

carlos: Customer provided curl of the final redirect they hit (server-side):

curl -i "https://callback.redwood.example/auth/callback?code=4/ABCDEFG&state=E2%26F%3D%20xyz&utm_source=redir"

Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"state_mismatch","expected":"E2%26F%3D%2Bxyz","received":"E2%26F%3D%20xyz"}

elaine: There it is: received has a space where we expected +. That implies a + was decoded to space by some layer. Our state compare should compare the raw querystring before any URL-decoding, or we should normalize both sides by applying application/x-www-form-urlencoded rules consistently.

mike (sre): Quick mitigation: treat spaces and + as equivalent for state compare for a short window (keeps compatibility). But must be careful not to open replay/CSRF holes. Limit to requests where code is present and nonce is valid.

sam (support): Also ask customer to set PKCE code_verifier length >= 43 and ensure code_challenge_method is S256. If webview or proxy modifies characters (+ vs - vs _) we might hit pkce mismatch too later.

carlos: Customer tried direct redirect (bypassing analytics) — success. So root cause = analytics redirector rewriting encoding. They control that proxy. They've agreed to change it to preserve percent-encoding (no decode/re-encode cycle).

elaine: For our side: will open a tiny patch to make state comparison tolerant to plus->space in querystring for oauth callback, with a monitoring flag and audit log. Also add doc note under OAuth best-practices: "do not decode fragment/query in intermediate redirectors".

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: branch oauth-state-tolerate-plus -> staging at 2026-03-18T02:15:00Z

sam (support): I'll follow up with the customer once patch is in staging and ask them to re-test. Add instructions: if using app webview, recommend SFSafariViewController instead of older UIWebView or custom webviews.

carlos: Thanks team — closing after verified with customer. :thumbsup:
